title: Exact Quantitative Laws for the Spectral Braess Paradox: Multiplicative Weyl Bounds, Degeneracy Immunity, and the Asymmetric Cheeger-Spectral Rift
abstract: Adding edges to a connected graph G always increases every eigenvalue of the combinatorial Laplacian L_G, yet it can paradoxically decrease the spectral gap lambda_2(G) of the normalized Laplacian L_norm(G) = I - D_G^{-1/2} A_G D_G^{-1/2}, slowing random-walk relaxation. We establish four exact quantitative laws governing this spectral Braess paradox: (1) Universal Multiplicative Weyl Inequality: for every connected non-complete graph G with minimum degree delta(G) >= r >= 1 and every edge-disjoint added graph H on V(G), lambda_j(G+H)/lambda_j(G) >= 1/(1 + rho(D_G^{-1/2} A_H D_G^{-1/2})) >= r/(r + rho(A_H)) for all lambda_j(G) <= 1, and identically for 2 - lambda_n(G+H) and the absolute spectral gap gamma_*(G) = min(lambda_2, 2 - lambda_n). Via Stanley's and Nosal-Nikiforov's spectral radius bounds, cliques K_t (sharp floor r/(r+t-1) on K_{r,m}+K_t) are globally optimal k-edge saboteurs and balanced bicliques K_{a,a} (sharp floor r/(r+a)) are optimal triangle-free saboteurs; (2) Exact Degeneracy Immunity: adding any d-degenerate graph H of arbitrary size and maximum degree satisfies lambda_j(G+H)/lambda_j(G) >= 1 - sqrt(d/(d+r)) = r/(r+d+sqrt(d(d+r))), sharp on K_{r,m}+K_{d,k} (1 << k << m) for every (d, r), implying size-independent immunity for forests (1 - 1/sqrt(2) ~ 0.2929), outerplanar graphs (1 - sqrt(2/3) ~ 0.1835), and planar graphs (1 - sqrt(5/6) ~ 0.0871); (3) Asymmetric Single-Edge Law and Cheeger-Spectral Rift: for an added edge e = {u, v} with degrees r < s, Cheeger conductance obeys phi(G+e)/phi(G) >= (r+s)/(r+s+2) whereas lambda_2 obeys a strict four-level hierarchy r/(r+1) < sqrt(rs)/(sqrt(rs)+1) < Psi(r,s;1) = 1 - 1/sqrt((r+1)(s+1)) < (r+s)/(r+s+2), realized asymptotically by clique-attachment graphs G_{r,s,M} while reconciling at (r+s)/(r+s+2) as lambda_2(G) -> 0+; and (4) Regular-Graph Localization Obstruction and Complete Equipartite Classification: connected r-regular graphs satisfy lambda_2(G+e)/lambda_2(G) >= Phi_reg(r, lambda_2) > r/(r+1) for all lambda_2 < 1, while at lambda_2 = 1 we classify all connected non-complete r-regular graphs as the complete equipartite graphs K_{m,...,m} (r=(k-1)m) and prove that K_{r,r}+e strictly minimizes lambda_2(G+e) among all of them, with unique global minimum (14 - sqrt(26))/10 ~ 0.8901 at K_{4,4}+e. The algebraic core (15 theorems) is formally certified in Lean 4.36.0 (zero sorry, zero grind, zero custom axioms).
